title: Part 2.IV — Agency and Purpose
triple_pass_note: Pass 1 = capture (verbatim chunk anchoring per subsection); Pass 2 = pentad operationalization (Agency + Purpose simultaneously, since this chapter does two terms); Pass 3 = cross-pipeline edges (Calleja PIM, Aristotle/Phantasia, Heidegger BCAP / Being and Time, Uexküll Foray, Rickert Ambient, Gross Uncomfortable, Hawhee pending).

outline.heading: The Philosophy of Means
outline.summary: Burke opens with Baldwin's 'tender Pragmatism' gloss (Kant hypothetical-imperative species prescribing means to happiness) and seizes the means-reference as warrant for the pipeline's diagnostic: Pragmatism is generated by the featuring of Agency as motive-locus. Dewey's Instrumentalism, William James's 'method only,' Peirce's 'beliefs as rules for action,' James's 'theories thus become instruments' — all are read as different surfaces of the same pentadic underlay. Burke distinguishes between (a) the trivial sense in which 'every philosophy needs a doctrine of means' (Stoic, Epicurean, Platonist, Kantian pragmatisms) and (b) the modern, science-driven sense in which agency-as-accumulating-power has risen to first place. Papini's corridor-in-a-hotel image (via James) makes pragmatism a principle of mediation common to all rooms.

outline.heading: Aristotle subordination + agency-as-ancestor
outline.summary: Aristotle's organon ('logic as instrument of human reason') is read as 'incipiently pragmatist,' but his slave-culture position subordinated agency among the four causes (material, efficient, formal, final). Modern science's non-Aristotelian element is exactly the inversion: agency becomes uppermost, final cause is played down, and 'whereas means were treated in terms of ends, ends become treated in terms of means.' Vocational training is the everyday case: 'because there are cars, some men learn to become automobile mechanics' — instrument as ancestor of life-purpose. Money supplies a derivative 'absolute purpose' over and above per-instrument purposes.

outline.heading: Emerson's incipient pragmatism
outline.summary: Burke reads Emerson's Nature (Commodity / Beauty / Language / Discipline) as transitional: agency has not yet become ancestral term but is still seen in terms of universal purpose. The 'In God, every end is converted into a new means' passage marks the seam — secular agency as function of divine purpose. Narrowing the circumference by dropping final cause is the move required to reach pragmatism proper.

outline.heading: Dewey + Mead biologism; Bridgman operationalism
outline.summary: Replace Emerson's transcendentalism and James's personalism with Dewey/Mead biologism (Experience and Nature; The Philosophy of the Act): biological functioning as a transitional device where bodily organs are means-toward-ends without theological or personalistic final cause. Pragmatism pure-and-simple = P. W. Bridgman's operationalism (Logic of Modern Physics): meaning equated with the corresponding set of operations. Burke's critique: Bridgman's own concepts (e.g. 'principle') are possible only to substantialist thought; he 'is writing about his purpose in eliminating the concept of purpose,' a state requiring an analysis his method cannot perform. The instrument has 'purpose imbedded in its structure and design' — it performs without purpose because it has purpose.

outline.heading: The Range of Pragmatism / Conditions
outline.summary: Burke traces 'conditions' from Aquinas (formal) through Kant (transcendental — conditions of experience) → Fichte (Ego/Non-Ego) → Hegel (Ausserung/Vermittlung as utterance/mediation) → Marx (material/economic conditions formative of spirit). Hegelian mediation (Vermittlung) explicitly anticipates pragmatism through idealism. But Marx is not 'pragmatist' because a strong sense of form pervades his history.

outline.heading: The Facts (documentary historiography)
outline.summary: Pragmatist history enters with the 'documentary' ideal: documentary-facts are the medium with which the historian works; writing 'pure document' places major stress on the medium itself — a featuring of agency. But essentialist demands surreptitiously return: the historian gives essences while disclaiming any such purpose.

outline.heading: Two Principles of Truth in James
outline.summary: James contains a conflict of dramatist and positivist ideals in his notion of truth. Burke locates James's pragmatism on the Grammatical fact that human acts are not 'verifiable' the way purely scenic statements are: 'The proof of a human act is in the doing.' Two verifications coexist in agency: (1) verification of an act by an act (belief tested by believing); (2) verification of an act-less scenic statement by an act framed in accordance with it (map tested by following). Agency is essentially mediatory — it can straddle act and event.

outline.heading: Symbolic of Agency
outline.summary: Instruments are 'essentially' human as products of human design. Burke threads a Symbolic-of-Motives argument: the agent-as-mother (the formative experience of personal utility in infancy → 'Mother Nature'); the Agency–Purpose grammar in sexual terms (maternal woman = utility; erotic woman = purpose; courtship's symbolic-incest task = transcending maternal utility); Bentham's 'crabbed bachelor' Utilitarianism as deflected erotic-purpose into maternal-agency; Baudelaire's La Géante as the merging of maternal/erotic principles. This Symbolic detour is explicitly bracketed: 'systematic consideration belongs rather in the Symbolic of Motives.'

outline.heading: Purposive Agencies of Applied Science
outline.summary: Agency's prestige derives first from the Grammatical fact that it covers applied science — the area of new power. Modern-scientific elimination of Purpose provokes shift to agency, the term nearest of kin, which 'can supply the functions of purpose even when the term is formally omitted as a locus of motives.' Reduction of action to motion = reduction to Agency; the action-motion ambiguity is conveniently straddled by Pragmatism. Money's 'cash-value' contributes; stock-market personifications ('it very frankly acts as if it wanted to have an old-fashioned reaction') reveal corporate-entity-as-agent. The chapter closes the Agency-half with a 'principle of entropy' image: philosophic schools level off toward their 'heat-death' in Pragmatism — Papini's corridor revisited.

outline.heading: Ends / Modifications of Purpose
outline.summary: Baldwin's Mysticism entry: 'immediate apprehension of the divine essence or the ultimate ground of existence,' identity with 'the Being of beings,' 'metaphysical fascination.' Burke argues: not mere unity but unity of the individual with some cosmic or universal Purpose is the mark of mysticism — confirmed by the fact that anti-vitalist/anti-teleological philosophies herald their attainments as the elimination of 'mysticism' and 'teleology.' Sociologically: mystic philosophies flourish in periods of confusion about human purpose. Paradox of substance: a purpose so 'pure' becomes much the same as no purpose at all; mystic oxymoron (black radiance, docta ignorantia, learned ignorance); the mystic's 'free' union with the All-Purpose is also a compulsion. Purpose has become 'the one most susceptible of dissolution,' yet survives implicitly in act, agent, and agency.

outline.heading: Purpose in Aristotle
outline.summary: EXEGETICAL Aristotle bridge. The most realistic synonym for purpose is Aristotelian eudaimonia ('happiness'), one level beneath Purpose itself. Burke cites Rhetoric I.5: 'Men, individually and in common, nearly all have some aim...' Topics of the deliberative orator are organized around this; men deliberate about means, not about the end. Good as 'whatever is desirable for its own sake, or for the sake of which we choose something else.' Virtues defined teleologically. Seven causes (chance, nature, compulsion, habit, reason, anger, desire) furnish oratorical commonplaces. 'Instruments are considered by Aristotle in teleological terms, as their form is said to be derived from the end desired by their users.' Living things: vegetative–sensitive–rational hierarchy of immanent purposes. Politics and Nicomachean Ethics both begin from teleological premise. Burke insists: this analysis is 'wholly realistic,' not mystical — only when purpose becomes total does it fit the mystical prescription.

outline.heading: Platonist and Neo-Platonist Purpose
outline.summary: Plato's equation Good = One brings purpose nearer to mysticism; Neo-Platonists (Plotinus, Enneads I.3) complete the mystic oxymoron in the dialectic of the Upward Way — 'Our journey is to the Good, to the Primal-Principle.' Korzybski's higher-and-higher levels of generalization map this. Reverse course: unity resolved into particulars infused with the spirit of the First. The First is beyond human comprehension except in mystic transcendence; otherwise it is the Absolute Good — 'the absolutizing of the concept of purpose.'

outline.heading: Physiology of Mysticism
outline.summary: Burke re-cites Permanence and Change: the mystic trance as a possible 'assertion in vacuo' — all conflicting nervous impulses called into play at once. Since directed muscular movement requires repression of competing impulses, the mystic trance may consist in stimulation of nerves without muscular movement: 'pure action / total passivity' — incipient-action without overt motor response. Burke now adds: this would amount to a kind of 'total purpose,' in a transcendent state of 'pre-motion.' This is the biological-substrate node of the chapter and the strongest anticipatory bridge to Uexküll Funktionskreis (Merk-/Wirk-organ coupling) and to BCAP's pathos / incipient affective tonality.

outline.heading: Purposiveness in the Negative
outline.summary: Spinoza's Mystical strain in Oneness/Allness despite his programmatic denial of Universal Purpose. Burke adds 'the negative' to his synonyms for Purpose, via mystical via negativa of negative theology. First Principle as highest level of generalization is endowed with negative attributes (infinite, incomprehensible, unending, incorporeal). Spinoza inverts: Universal Substance positive, determinate Modes as negation — 'all determination is negation.' Bergson's Creative Evolution: negative as a function of desire/expectation/interest; the 'it is not' implies a positive condition. Burke dramatistically revises: the origin of the negative is not informational but moral — 'thou shalt not' of the Decalogue, not 'it is not.' Greek/Latin verbs of fear taking negative forms for positive states (vereor ne veniat). Negative theology begins in fear/apprehension prior to the 'semantic' negative.

outline.heading: Unity and the Reflexive
outline.summary: Mystic unity = communion = unification = transcending of disunity → reflexive doublings everywhere. Melville's Pierre (incest/self-abuse imagery); James's Xenos Clark (anaesthetic revelation almost catching up with himself, kissing his own lips); Nietzsche's eternal-recurrence as cosmic replica; Eliot's Murder in the Cathedral wheel-and-still-centre as duplication of poet↔critic; Little Gidding's Midwinter spring as 'transition made permanent' / Santayana-essence; Shelley's Alastor (poet-on-foot → boat-trance → stream that 'imagest my life'). Reflexivity is the formal mark of the mystic Self.

outline.heading: Mysticism and Idealism: The Self
outline.summary: Going from Purpose → Unity → Self shows how Mysticism and Idealism reinforce each other. Self is properly under the sign of Agent, but as super-self / non-self it acquires the same universalized quality noted in the mystic paradox where absolute purpose becomes necessity. Burke cites Symonds-via-James: progressive obliteration of space, time, sensation — 'pure, absolute, abstract Self.' Kant's synthetic unity of apperception, Shelley's anonymous wanderer = verbal equivalents of universalized first-person. The transcendent Self is genetically (collectively, linguistically) human, not individually.

outline.heading: Images and the 'Demonic Trinity'
outline.summary: Images can lead to mystical transcendence by generalizing role until dramatist 'people in situations' retreats behind pure lyric of imagistic succession. Survey of purposive imagery: 'vocation/calling' (voice within); Meredith's thought-as-bell; door-opening/shutting half-asleep; change-of-scene as change-of-motive; knocking as deterrent purpose; scapegoats; pollution-imagery in mystic drought. The 'demonic trinity' = erotic + urinary + excremental, united in the cloacal; rain may serve vicariously for urination and erotic-purpose; 'excremental' invective allows translation of erotic purpose from 'love' to 'war.' Mystic thoroughness requires recognition of fundamental taboos at the very moment of their transcendence.

outline.heading: Silence and the Hunt
outline.summary: At the centre of mobility is the purpose of the hunt; hence imagery of the desired as that for which we 'hunger.' Twelfth Night opening (hart/heart pun) and Rousseau's Emile (hunt as stage prior to sexual quest) double-motivate the body. Mystic silence has its roots in the purposive: in the quest one is naturally silent — animal stalking quarry or thinker meditating an idea — even the utterance of the question begins in the silence of the quest. Socratic questioning; Hamlet's 'the rest is silence.' Three aspects of the ineffable: (i) Korzybski's 'unspeakable' (rites of desanctification as first mystical appreciation of powers in things — word-magic as deteriorated form of original distrust of words); (ii) ineffability of visceral processes; (iii) ineffability of linguistic relations themselves.

outline.heading: The Mystic 'Moment'
outline.summary: Unity ≠ First: passing the tenth floor on the way up differs from passing it on the way down (nine-plus-one ≠ eleven-minus-one). The dialectic of the Upward Way proceeds by stages until a generalization-level not originally envisaged is reached, whereupon particulars look different in light of this 'higher vision' — the Grammar of rebirth. Proust's many-moments-one (peacock's tail); the mysticism of gambling (pure-purpose communing with fate); Dostoevsky's 'representative accident' (father's death) and Raskolnikov (Crime and Punishment) — the murder as 'absolute' act 'conceived independently of its conditions,' a 'representative' act seeking the essence of power (pure purpose). Crime produces 'oneness with the universe' via universal persecution — the teleological view 'lost by evolutionism' returns in criminal guilt.

outline.heading: Mysticism of Means
outline.summary: The 'moment' is to what follows as implicit is to explicit, as deus implicitus to deus explicitus. Pragmatist-kind-of-mysticism: Aldous Huxley's pacifism ('impure acts must follow from impure means' — only by peaceful means can we get peace). Burke critiques: peace-as-end then becomes either impossible or unnecessary. All means are necessarily impure (they bear properties for other possible uses, including hostile uses); 'we act by a progressive purification of them.' From the dramatistic standpoint, ends do not simply result from means: 'a statement when confined to terms of means and end eliminates act as a special locus of motives by treating the act simply as means to an end.' Action overlaps with being: 'a way of being is substantival, not instrumental.' America's pragmatist objection to socialism ('wouldn't work') shifts to idealist/realist 'not the American way' once Soviet resistance demonstrates workability — 'pure mysticism' of nationalism. Thomas à Kempis Imitation of Christ as Upward Way transformed into monastic discipline: 'In all things behold the end,' contemning of the world as means.

outline.heading: Rationalism and the Verbal Medium
outline.summary: Baldwin: rationalism = (1) religion to be rationally explained or rejected; (2) reason as independent source of knowledge with higher authority than sense-perception; (3) elementary concepts from which all is to be derived deductively. Descartes (Discourse on Method), Spinoza (Ethics more geometrico), Leibniz (universal logic-and-language); Hegel pushes farthest: the world is Reason. Rationalism is forerunner to pragmatism in its stress on method, but they become opposed because empiricism opposes rationalism and pragmatism aligns with empiricism. Burke's synthesis: in rationalism end is implicit in beginning; the present sums up the past and implicitly contains the future (Leibniz's accurate statement about his own books). Santayana's equating of mathematics and dialectic on grounds of internal development. Burke's own Grammar declares itself 'rationalistic in this dialectical sense' — explicit approach to language as dialectical structure — and 'empiricist' in recognizing every linguistic structure as a new thing; 'spinning five terms into a book, by making their implications explicit.' Money's monetary-rationality and capitalist symbolism (investment as 'incipient act' / 'representative moment' of delay); St Ambrose's debt-ransom Christology as resonance of monetary-religious atonement; psychoanalytic repression as 'cameo/intaglio' reciprocal of purpose ('negative purpose').

outline.heading: Means and Ends of This Grammar
outline.summary: The five pentadic terms are 'transcendental rather than formal (and are to this extent Kantian)' — necessary 'forms of talk about experience' rather than 'forms of experience.' Burke's project is the analysis of language, not of 'reality.' Closing program: neo-Stoic cosmopolitanism (tolerance, resignation to bureaucratic requirements of modern industry/commerce) against fanaticism and dissipation. The needed attitude is 'mildly hypochondriasis' / 'cultural valetudinarianism' (gymnastic + clinic of ideas). The book's motto: Ad Bellum Purificandum — 'Towards the Purification of War.' Method's substantiation-transubstantiation distinction sets up Part III: Constitutions for substantiation; transubstantiation as 'representative moment of dialectic in general.'

concepts.definition: Burke's diagnostic identification: pragmatism is the philosophic school recognizable by its raising of Agency (means, instrument, method) to first place among the five terms; Dewey's Instrumentalism, James's 'method only,' Peirce's beliefs-as-rules-for-action are surfaces of this featuring.

Modern science's non-Aristotelian inversion of the four-cause hierarchy: where Aristotle treated means in terms of ends, pragmatism treats ends in terms of means; vocational training (the auto-mechanic learning his vocation 'because there are cars') is the canonical case.

P. W. Bridgman's Logic of Modern Physics: meaning equated with the corresponding set of operations; two procedures for measuring the same temperature count 'in principle' as two concepts; the limit-case of pragmatism pure-and-simple.

Burke's grammatical correction to operationalism: instruments perform without purpose because they have purpose imbedded in their structure and design — they can do their work 'merely by continuing to be themselves' precisely because of inherited human purpose.

Hegelian Ausserung (utterance) of the internal principle as Vermittlung (mediation) — the genealogy by which idealism becomes a precursor of pragmatism; Marx particularizes by treating economic conditions as formative of spirit but retains a strong sense of form alien to true pragmatism.

The documentary ideal of historiography — recording 'whatever historical events are known to have occurred together' — features agency because documents are the medium with which the historian works; essentialist demands return surreptitiously.

concepts.concept: Two principles of verification in James
concepts.definition: (1) verification of an act by an act (believing as test of belief); (2) verification of an act-less scenic statement by an act framed in accordance with it (map tested by following). Agency mediates between dramatist act-talk and positivist event-talk.

Pragmatism's advantage over Materialism is that the reduction of action to motion can be re-described as reduction to Agency; tools are 'more purposive' than impersonal backgrounds, so the agency-locus straddles the action–motion fissure.

concepts.concept: Corporate entity as agent (Papini corridor + stock-market 'it')
concepts.definition: Pragmatism as 'corridor common to all rooms' (Papini-via-James) and the financial-page personification ('it very frankly acts as if it wanted...') both display agency-language's tendency to constitute corporate agents from impersonal aggregates.

concepts.concept: Entropy / heat-death of philosophic schools in Pragmatism
concepts.definition: Burke's closing trope for the Agency-half: a 'second law of thermodynamics' image — philosophic distinctions level off toward their heat-death in Pragmatism, which is the entropic mediator-form among the five featurings.

Burke's diagnostic identification: mysticism is the philosophic school recognizable by its featuring of Purpose (universal end, the One, divine telos) as motive-locus; 'not mere unity but unity of the individual with some cosmic or universal purpose' is the mark; teleology-as-eliminated-target confirms by contrast.

concepts.concept: Paradox of pure purpose (oxymoron / docta ignorantia)
concepts.definition: A purpose so 'pure' becomes much the same as no purpose at all — mystic oxymorons (black radiance, bitter sweetness, learned ignorance) and the mystic's 'free' union with the All-Purpose as compulsion; absolute Purpose passes into mechanism (perfect regularity as Creator's 'design').

concepts.concept: Eudaimonia as realistic synonym for Purpose (EXEGETICAL Aristotle)
concepts.definition: Aristotelian happiness, one level of generalization beneath Purpose itself; Rhetoric I.5 frames the topoi about this aim; deliberative orator concerned with means; good = 'desirable for its own sake, or for the sake of which we choose something else.'

Aristotelian living-thing hierarchy: vegetative–sensitive–appetitive–rational, each adding immanent purposes; instruments teleologically receive their form from the end desired by their users; Politics and Nicomachean Ethics both built on this premise.

Neo-Platonist dialectic toward the Primal-Principle: ascent to higher generalizations until Unity; descent re-infusing particulars with the spirit of the First; mystic transcendence as the only access to the First-beyond-discourse.

concepts.concept: Physiology of mysticism / pure action as pre-motion
concepts.definition: Mystic trance hypothesised as nervous-impulse-without-muscular-movement: conflicting impulses 'glow' simultaneously because incipient stage requires no inhibition; 'a kind of total purpose, in a transcendent state of pre-motion.'

Negative theology's apophatic predicates (infinite, incomprehensible, incorporeal) flow from the First's status as highest generalization; Spinoza's 'all determination is negation' inverts; Bergson's 'negative as function of desire/expectation' is dramatistically revised by Burke to 'thou shalt not' of the Decalogue.

Mystic communion as transcending-of-disunity that requires doubling: Xenos Clark almost kissing his own lips, Nietzsche's eternal recurrence as cosmic-replica of moment, Shelley's Alastor-poet finding stream 'imagest my life,' Eliot's wheel-with-still-centre.

Burke's image-cluster for the cloacal-mystical: three bodily principles vicariously substitutable for one another (rain↔urination↔erotic-purpose); 'thinking of the body' as condition of poetic transcendence; ecclesia super cloacam.

concepts.concept: Hunt as biological substrate of purposive language
concepts.definition: 'At the very centre of mobility is the purpose of the hunt' — hunger for the desired; mystic silence rooted in the quest (animal stalking, thinker meditating); even questions begin in the silence of the quest; Socratic questioning, Hamlet's silence, Korzybski's rites of desanctification, ineffability of visceral processes and of linguistic relations themselves.

The temporal-grammatical signature of mystic conversion: a generalization-level not originally envisaged is reached, after which all particulars look different in its light; nine-plus-one ≠ eleven-minus-one in the elevator; Proust's many-moments-one; the criminal's 'representative' act (Raskolnikov) conceived independently of its conditions.

Burke's diagnosis of Aldous Huxley: doctrine that impure acts must follow from impure means treats means as ancestor of ends (deus implicitus / explicitus). Burke critiques: all means are necessarily impure (they have properties for other uses); progressive purification, not means-end identity; action is also a way of being, substantival, not instrumental.

Money figures simultaneously as agency (medium) and as purpose (cash-value, profit-motive); the 'mysticism of money' (Harold Loeb); capitalist investment as 'incipient act' / 'representative moment' of delayed consumption; St Ambrose's ransom-Christology resonance; psychoanalysis as secular variant of negative theology.

'Towards the Purification of War' — Burke's own motto for the Grammar; war cannot be eliminated from an organism with combat-motives in its essence but can be refined toward a more peaceful war than the present peace; the book's project as the linguistic-critical purification of motive-talk.

The five pentadic terms are 'transcendental rather than formal (and are to this extent Kantian)' — necessary forms of talk-about-experience rather than forms of experience itself; Burke's project is the analysis of language, not of 'reality.'

Psychoanalytic repression is 'the reciprocal of purpose' — purpose rephrased in terms of post-Christian liberalism; psychoanalysis as a secular negative theology; Freudian system organized about the purposive as fully as Aristotle, with dialectical laws of its sublimation/compulsion-translation.

Burke's hypothesis: as evolutionary/non-purposive forms of expression are learned, teleological 'experience' survives implicitly — 'Grammatical repression'; the child's 'What are the hills for?' is corrected to 'How do the hills come to be?' but teleological intent may survive vestigially beneath the evolutionary style.

On the Symbolic level, the human being's first formative experience of personal utility is in the person of the mother → 'Mother Nature' → Bentham's bachelor utilitarianism as deflected erotic-purpose / Symbolic castration in his neutral scientific vocabulary.

Three aspects of the ineffable: (i) Korzybski's unspeakable level of things-themselves and rites of desanctification; (ii) ineffability of visceral processes (no sensation describable to one who has not experienced it); (iii) ineffability of linguistic relations themselves — any explication produces a new level of implication.

concepts.concept: Catholic/Protestant/Scientist as Act/Agent/Scene voices + money across
concepts.definition: Burke's compressed three-voices reading: 'Catholic act, Protestant agent, Scientist scene,' with money 'lying across the three, indeterminately Agent or Purpose' — the chapter's culminating compression of pentad-philosophic-school mapping prior to the Means-and-Ends close.

agency_term_operationalization.definition_le80_words: Agency is Burke's pentadic term for the means, instruments, methods, mediating media through which an act is brought about. Its diagnostic question is 'How? By what means?' As motive-locus it features in pragmatism: action explained by the medium that mediates it. Burke distinguishes Agency from Agent (Agency is impersonal mediation; Agent is personal locus) and from Act (Agency is means; Act is the doing). Modern science's elimination of final cause raises Agency to ancestral term, with money as paradigm.
agency_term_operationalization.question: How? By what means?
exemplars_in_chapter: William James (method only; cash-value; menial services)
John Dewey (Instrumentalism; Experience and Nature)
G. H. Mead (Philosophy of the Act; the 'other' whose attitudes we dialectically include)
Peirce (beliefs as rules for action)
P. W. Bridgman (operationalism; Logic of Modern Physics)
Aristotle (organon — 'incipiently pragmatist' but subordinated)
Emerson (incipient pragmatism via Nature's Commodity/Beauty/Language/Discipline)
Bentham (utilitarianism / 'fig-leaves')
agency_term_operationalization.calleja_pim_rationale: Agency = how-by-what-means maps cleanly onto Calleja's PIM Kinesthetic dimension (controls / motor mediation between player and game-state) and onto the Ludic dimension (rules as the instrumental system through which play-acts are made possible). The Bridgman operationalism passage — meaning equated with operations — is the Burke-side anchor for kinesthetic-input as constitutive of the act-described. The 'instrument has purpose embedded in its structure and design' is the strongest anticipatory anchor: game-mechanics carry designer-purpose that the player exercises without needing to articulate that purpose.
agency_term_operationalization.uexkull_mapping: Merk-/Wirk-organ pairing (receptor + effector poles of the functional cycle)
agency_term_operationalization.uexkull_rationale: Uexküll's Funktionskreis pairs a Merk-Organ (perception-organ → Merkwelt) with a Wirk-Organ (effect-organ → Wirkwelt) coupled through the object-as-Merkmal/Wirkmal-carrier. This receptor/effector instrumentation is structurally the agency-pole of the biosemiotic loop: how the animal-subject reaches into its Umwelt. The Burke 'physiology of mysticism' / 'pre-motion' incipient-action passages — nervous impulses 'glowing' without muscular discharge — are the anticipatory anchor: Burke independently arrives at a receptor-effector decoupling description of mystic 'pure action.' Provenance: anticipatory-projection (Burke 1945 has 0 Uexküll hits volume-wide).
agency_term_operationalization.ontological_grounding_rationale: Burke himself reads Aristotle's organon as 'incipiently pragmatist' (book p. 276) but emphasizes Aristotle's subordination of agency under final cause. The dissertation's anchor of Agency to Aristotelian technē (craft / productive knowledge with its own internal aitia) is therefore ANTICIPATORY-PROJECTION rather than exegetical: Burke does not himself develop technē as the proper home of agency. Technē supplies the missing ontological grounding for agency-as-rule-bound-mediation (the instrument 'has purpose imbedded in its structure and design') that Burke gestures toward but does not name.
agency_term_operationalization.forward_reference_to_rhetoric_of_motives: Burke's 'incipient act' / 'attitude' formulations in this chapter (the coin tossed to the leper as the 'humanitarian ambiguity ... of the attitude, the incipient act,' book p. 314) anticipate the sixth pentad term — Attitude — added in A Rhetoric of Motives (1950). Agency-as-attitude is the Rhetoric-of-Motives extension that the Grammar leaves implicit.
agency_term_operationalization.dissertation_use: Game-studies theories that feature controls/affordances/rule-systems as the locus of player-motive (procedural rhetoric — Bogost; instrumental-play — Aarseth's ergodic literature; ludology in its strict form) are pragmatist-Agency theories in Burke's diagnostic. The dissertation can deploy GM-07 to characterize any 'how the game is played' theory as a pragmatist featuring of Agency; conversely, the Burke critique (Bridgman's substantialist 'principle'; the impossibility of writing about 'purpose in eliminating purpose') generalizes into a critique of any closed instrumental account of play.

purpose_term_operationalization.definition_le80_words: Purpose is Burke's pentadic term for the end, telos, motivating-toward-which of an act. Its diagnostic question is 'Why?' As motive-locus it features in mysticism: action explained by the cosmic end toward which it is drawn. Burke's mark of mysticism is 'unity of the individual with some cosmic or universal purpose,' not mere unity. Pure Purpose collapses into the paradox-of-substance (docta ignorantia), into mechanism, into the negative; it survives implicitly even where formally eliminated.
purpose_term_operationalization.question: Why?

purpose_term_operationalization.calleja_pim_rationale: Purpose = why maps onto Calleja's PIM Ludic dimension (game-goal pursuit as the motive-engine of play) and onto the Narrative dimension (story-arc as the teleological closure that gives in-game-action its meaning). Burke's 'unity of the individual with some cosmic or universal purpose' is the structural template for game-narrative-immersion: the player's individual purpose absorbed into the universal purpose-design of the story-world. The dissertation can deploy Burke's paradox-of-pure-purpose to diagnose 'narrative-only' game theories as mystical featurings of Purpose that risk dissolving into either mechanism (the rails-narrative) or compulsion (the absolutized telos).
purpose_term_operationalization.uexkull_mapping: Closure of functional loop on biological need / valenced object
purpose_term_operationalization.uexkull_rationale: Uexküll's Funktionskreis closes when the receptor/effector cycle terminates on a Bedeutungsträger (meaning-carrier) keyed to a biological need (food, mate, threat-avoidance). This closure-toward-valenced-object is the purpose-pole of the biosemiotic cycle. Burke's 'Silence and the Hunt' subsection — 'at the very centre of mobility is the purpose of the hunt; hence the imagery of the desired as that for which we hunger' — independently arrives at the same convergence of biological need, motoric quest, and meaning-laden object. Provenance: anticipatory-projection (Burke 1945 has 0 Uexküll hits volume-wide).
purpose_term_operationalization.ontological_grounding: Aristotelian telos + Heideggerian Worumwillen — ANTICIPATORY for Heidegger; EXEGETICAL for Aristotle (Burke has 'Purpose in Aristotle' subsection)
purpose_term_operationalization.ontological_grounding_rationale: Burke himself devotes a named subsection ('Purpose in Aristotle,' book pp. 292-293) to Aristotelian teleological purpose-as-eudaimonia, walking through Rhetoric I.5, Nicomachean Ethics I.1, and Politics I.1 with explicit citation; this is the EXEGETICAL anchor. Burke insists this analysis is 'wholly realistic' and not mystical — only total purpose fits the mystical prescription. The Heideggerian Worumwillen (for-the-sake-of-which, Being and Time §18 / §69) is the ANTICIPATORY anchor: Burke 1945 has 0 Heidegger hits and predates Macquarrie–Robinson by 17 years; the Worumwillen-Purpose convergence is parallel-discovery, not influence.
purpose_term_operationalization.forward_reference_to_rhetoric_of_motives: Burke's mystic-moment / representative-act passages (Raskolnikov, Proust, the criminal's universal-persecution-as-teleology-recovered) thematize attitude-toward-purpose; the Rhetoric of Motives Attitude as sixth pentad term explicitly grammaticizes this implicit dimension. The chapter's Symbolic-of-Motives bracket ('systematic consideration belongs rather in the Symbolic of Motives,' book p. 285) reserves the further development.
purpose_term_operationalization.dissertation_use: Game-studies theories that feature narrative arc, achievement-telos, or transcendent player-motivation as the locus of motive (narratology; transcendent-flow theories descended from Csikszentmihalyi; goal-directed achievement frameworks) are mystic-Purpose theories in Burke's diagnostic. The dissertation can deploy Burke's diagnostic that Purpose is 'the most susceptible of dissolution' and re-emerges where formally eliminated to argue that ludic-theories that purport to be purposeless (pure-Agency theories) covertly retain Purpose in their design-intent (Bridgman's 'principle').

mysticism.burke_critique: Pure Purpose passes into the paradox-of-substance (compulsion, mechanism); mysticism arrives at the same narrowing-of-circumference as materialism by absolutizing Purpose into fatality; mysticism + idealism reinforce each other in the abstract Self; mysticism-of-means (Huxley pacifism) is Burke's specifically critiqued limit-case.

rationalism.burke_treatment: Rationalism stands as forerunner to pragmatism in its stress on method; pragmatism aligns with empiricism (rationalism's opponent), generating an apparent contradiction Burke resolves by distinguishing rationalist dialectic (end implicit in beginning) from empiricist dialectic. Burke declares his own Grammar 'rationalistic in this dialectical sense' — spinning five terms into a book by making their implications explicit.

philosophic_school_mapping.non_bijective_note: Burke's diagnostic is featuring, not exclusivity: pragmatism deploys all five terms while featuring Agency; mysticism deploys all five while featuring Purpose. The dissertation can deploy this non-bijection for game-studies (a theory features one term but typically deploys all five).

positions.position: Pragmatism is generated by the featuring of Agency as motive-locus.
positions.burke_stance: diagnostic / structural — Burke's whole Part-2 philosophic-school mapping rests on this claim.

positions.position: Modern science's non-Aristotelian element is exactly Aristotle's subordination of agency under final cause being inverted; means become ancestors of ends.

positions.position: Instruments perform without purpose because they have purpose imbedded in their structure and design — Bridgman's operationalism cannot describe its own grammatical commitments.
Mysticism's mark is unity of the individual with cosmic or universal Purpose, not mere unity.
positions.burke_stance: diagnostic / structural — corrective to standard 'mysticism = unity' description.

positions.position: Aristotelian eudaimonia is the most realistic synonym for Purpose — purposive without being mystical; only when purpose becomes total does it fit the mystical prescription.
positions.burke_stance: exegetical, with a sharp boundary-claim against assimilating Aristotle to mysticism.

positions.position: Mysticism and Materialism converge by narrowing motivational circumference — Materialism by deliberate elimination of purpose, Mysticism by absolutizing purpose into fatality; 'motivational schemes that would feature it less may allow it more.'

All means are necessarily impure (they bear properties for other possible uses); 'we act by a progressive purification of them.' Action is also a way of being, substantival, not instrumental — Huxley's pacifism collapses ends into means.
The five pentadic terms are transcendental rather than formal — necessary forms of talk-about-experience, not forms of experience; the Grammar analyzes language, not 'reality.'
positions.burke_stance: self-reflexive methodological statement — Burke's own Grammar declares itself dialectical-rationalist plus empiricist.

positions.position: The book's motto Ad Bellum Purificandum frames its method as humanistic-contemplative purification of motive-talk; neo-Stoic cosmopolitanism against fanaticism and dissipation.
positions.burke_stance: programmatic / closing — orients the whole pentad-architecture toward Part 3 (Constitutions; transubstantiation).

positions.position: Psychoanalytic repression is 'the reciprocal of purpose' — the Freudian system organized about the purposive as fully as Aristotle, a secular variant of negative theology.
positions.burke_stance: synthesizing — purpose survives implicitly in modern 'rationalist' vocabularies that purport to eliminate it.

tensions.tension: Bridgman's operationalism declares its own purposelessness in purpose-laden vocabulary
tensions.description: Bridgman 'is writing about his purpose in eliminating the concept of purpose' (book p. 280). The operationalist program requires a substantialist 'principle' that operationalism cannot ground. Burke's Grammar exposes this as the structural fissure within pragmatism-pure-and-simple.

tensions.tension: Mysticism and Materialism converge by narrowing of circumference
tensions.description: Mysticism makes purpose absolute and thereby transforms it into fatality / mechanism; Materialism deliberately eliminates purpose. Both narrow motivational circumference. 'Ironically, motivational schemes that would feature it less may allow it more' (book p. 291).

tensions.tension: Purpose is 'the one most susceptible of dissolution' yet survives implicitly in act, agent, and agency
tensions.description: Modern materialist-behaviorist reduction eliminates purpose, yet pragmatism's appeal partly resides in implicit retention of purpose in agency. Burke calls this 'Grammatical repression' (book p. 290).

tensions.tension: Aristotelian eudaimonia is purposive but realistic, not mystical
tensions.description: Burke insists the strongly purposive ingredient in Aristotle is 'wholly realistic, as realistic as the vocabulary of proverbs'; only total purpose fits the mystical prescription. The Purpose-in-Aristotle subsection therefore EXEGETICALLY bridges Burke to Aristotle while resisting any mystic-Aristotle assimilation.

tensions.tension: Huxley's mysticism-of-means collapses ends into means
tensions.description: All means are necessarily impure; only progressive purification, not means-end identity, applies. 'A statement when confined to terms of means and end eliminates act as a special locus of motives' (book p. 310). Action is a way of being, substantival, not instrumental.

tensions.tension: Rationalism is forerunner to pragmatism in method-stress yet dialectically opposed via empiricism
tensions.description: Pragmatism, aligned with empiricism (rationalism's opponent), nonetheless inherits the method-featuring from rationalism. Burke resolves by distinguishing rationalist dialectic (end implicit in beginning) from empiricist dialectic, and declares his own Grammar both rationalistic and empiricist.

tensions.tension: Mysticism and Idealism reinforce each other through the abstract Self
tensions.description: Purpose → Unity → Self: Self is properly under Agent but the super-self / non-self acquires the mystic-paradox property whereby absolute purpose becomes necessity. Kant's synthetic unity of apperception, Shelley's anonymous wanderer = universalized first-person.

tensions.tension: Money is indeterminately Agent or Purpose
tensions.description: Burke's three-voices compression ('Catholic act, Protestant agent, Scientist scene') leaves money 'lying across the three, indeterminately Agent or Purpose' — the chapter's most compact statement of the agency-purpose collapse in capitalist modernity.

Symbolic-of-Agency / instrument-as-extension-of-agent; the mother-as-first-utility; agency 'essentially human' as product of design.

Action-motion ambiguity straddled by pragmatism; scenic materials become means in process of growth/adaptation; empiricism conforms to agency's mediatory genius.
Mysticism's primary ratio; the act conceived absolutely (Raskolnikov); criminal communion with cosmic motives.
Mysticism and Idealism: the Self — super-self as universalized agent; Kant's synthetic unity of apperception.
Cosmic circumference: Upward Way; First/Primal-Principle as scenic-purpose limit.
